summary: Summit lookout above Wallace, Idaho: log cabin 1916, concrete base with R-6 cab 1957, destroyed 1975; the base now holds communications gear.

facts.design: Concrete two-story base with R-6 flat cab (1957)
facts.status_note: Cab destroyed in 1975; the concrete base now houses communications equipment

visit.trail_note: A 2020 hike guide describes a route that starts on logging roads and leads uphill to a gate signed restricted access. No source says whether the public may use it.

corrections.proposed: R-6 flat cab on concrete two-story base (1957)
corrections.why: The L-4 cab was the cab moved from Maple Peak in 1950. The cab that replaced it in 1957 was an R-6 flat cab on a concrete base.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the base cinder block; the Idaho site says its lower floor is concrete. Both say the base now holds electronic or communications equipment.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 129.2 has no support in any source read. The lookout was a cab on a concrete base and no height is given, so the value should probably be cleared; it is not written as a correction because no replacement value exists. The Idaho list names Howard Crist in the early 1980s, after the 1975 destruction; left out of events and flagged in the story. Access is not stated by any source; the 2020 hike guide describes a gate signed restricted access on the approach, so the access level is left unset. Record elevation 1958 m matches the register (6,424 ft).
